answer: An agent economy can make each participant post a refundable bond before it can place orders, with reputation and access earned only after counterparties complete repeated, independently verified trades. A sybil can still create many names, but each must lock real capital, and splitting one identity into many does not multiply the bond’s purchasing power. Disputes slash the bond, so fake trades risk measurable loss. A velvet interface or pearl badge is no substitute: the bridge to influence is costly collateral and proven delivery.
